questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is urbanisation?

options.A: The process by which an increasing share of a country's population lives in urban settlements, accompanied by expansion of towns and cities and changes in economic and social activity
options.B: The movement of people from urban to rural areas
options.C: The construction of roads and buildings in villages

questions.explanation: Urbanisation is the process by which an increasing share of a country's population lives in urban settlements, accompanied by expansion of towns and cities and changes in economic and social activity.

options.B: Only census towns

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is a statutory town?

options.B: A settlement meeting Census criteria for urban character but not governed by a statutory urban local body

questions.subject: Development Issues

options.A: No. An ore is material from which a useful mineral or metal can be extracted economically
options.B: Yes. All minerals are ores
options.C: No. An ore is a synthetic material
options.D: Yes. An ore is any rock found underground

questions.explanation: Not all minerals are ores. An ore is material from which a useful mineral or metal can be extracted economically under prevailing conditions.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Is land degradation identical to desertification?

options.A: No. Desertification is land degradation specifically in drylands
options.B: Yes. Both are exactly the same
options.C: No. Desertification is broader than land degradation
options.D: Yes. Desertification means the spread of deserts only

questions.explanation: Land degradation is a broader concept, while desertification is land degradation specifically in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Is waste-to-energy always harmless?

options.A: No. It requires suitable waste composition, emission controls, residue management and regulatory compliance
options.B: Yes. Waste-to-energy is always harmless

questions.explanation: Waste-to-energy is not always harmless; it requires suitable waste composition, emission controls, residue management and regulatory compliance.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Is recycling the first priority in the waste hierarchy?

options.A: No. Prevention and reduction come first, followed by reuse, recycling and recovery
options.B: Yes. Recycling is the first priority
options.C: No. Disposal is the first priority

questions.explanation: In the waste hierarchy, prevention and reduction come first, followed by reuse, recycling and recovery.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Are nuclear and renewable energy the same category?

options.A: No. Nuclear is non-fossil but generally not renewable
options.B: Yes. Nuclear energy is renewable
options.D: No. Nuclear energy is a fossil fuel

questions.explanation: Nuclear energy is non-fossil but generally not renewable because it relies on finite nuclear fuels.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Does installed capacity equal actual electricity generation?

options.A: No. Capacity is rated power; generation is actual energy produced over time
options.B: Yes. Installed capacity equals actual generation
options.C: No. Capacity is actual energy; generation is rated power
options.D: Yes. Both are measured in MWh

questions.explanation: Installed capacity is rated power, while generation is actual energy produced over time.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Does economic growth automatically mean sustainable development?

options.A: No. Sustainability also requires social inclusion, resource efficiency, environmental protection and intergenerational equity
options.B: Yes. Economic growth always means sustainable development
options.C: No. Sustainable development means only environmental protection
options.D: Yes. Economic growth and sustainability are the same

questions.explanation: Economic growth does not automatically mean sustainable development; sustainability also requires social inclusion, resource efficiency, environmental protection and intergenerational equity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for a census town under Census 2011?

options.A: Population of at least 5,000
options.B: Density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre
options.C: At least 75% of male main workers engaged in non-agricultural pursuits

questions.explanation: A census town does not require a municipal corporation. The three criteria are population of at least 5,000, density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre, and at least 75% of male main workers engaged in non-agricultural pursuits.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a push factor of rural-to-urban migration?

options.A: Employment opportunities
options.B: Higher wages

questions.explanation: Rural unemployment is a push factor. Employment, higher wages and better education are pull factors.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a pull factor of urban migration?

options.A: Rural unemployment
options.B: Landlessness

questions.explanation: Employment opportunities are a pull factor. Rural unemployment, landlessness and drought are push factors.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive effect of urbanisation?

options.A: Housing shortages
options.B: Slums

questions.explanation: Larger markets and economic diversification are positive effects of urbanisation. Housing shortages, slums and congestion are problems of unplanned urbanisation.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a problem of unplanned urbanisation?

options.A: Productivity gains
options.B: Innovation

questions.explanation: Housing shortages and slums are problems of unplanned urbanisation. Productivity gains, innovation and economies of scale are positive effects.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an agro-based industry?

options.A: Iron and steel
options.B: Cement

questions.explanation: Sugar is an agro-based industry. Iron and steel, cement and aluminium are mineral-based industries.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a mineral-based industry?

options.A: Cotton textiles
options.B: Food processing

questions.explanation: Cement is a mineral-based industry. Cotton textiles, food processing and sugar are agro-based industries.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an adverse effect of poorly regulated industrialisation?

options.A: Employment generation
options.B: Technology transfer

questions.explanation: Air and water pollution is an adverse effect of poorly regulated industrialisation. Employment generation, technology transfer and export growth are benefits.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social infrastructure?

options.A: Roads
options.B: Railways

questions.explanation: Healthcare is an example of social infrastructure. Roads, railways and ports are economic infrastructure.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of economic infrastructure?

options.A: Education
options.B: Healthcare

questions.explanation: Transport is an example of economic infrastructure. Education, healthcare and housing are social infrastructure.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of hard infrastructure?

options.A: Education
options.B: Healthcare

questions.explanation: Roads are an example of hard infrastructure. Education, healthcare and governance are soft infrastructure.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of soft infrastructure?

options.A: Railways
options.B: Ports

questions.explanation: Education is an example of soft infrastructure. Railways, ports and power plants are hard infrastructure.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a metallic mineral?

options.A: Limestone
options.B: Mica

questions.explanation: Iron ore is a metallic mineral. Limestone, mica and gypsum are non-metallic minerals.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-metallic mineral?

options.A: Bauxite
options.B: Manganese

questions.explanation: Limestone is a non-metallic mineral. Bauxite, manganese and copper are metallic minerals.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental impact of mining?

options.A: Employment generation
options.B: Royalty revenue

questions.explanation: Water contamination is an environmental impact of mining. Employment generation, royalty revenue and export earnings are economic benefits.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a human cause of land degradation?

options.A: Drought
options.B: Intense rainfall

questions.explanation: Deforestation is a human cause of land degradation. Drought, intense rainfall and floods are natural causes.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a natural cause of land degradation?

options.A: Overgrazing
options.B: Unsustainable farming

questions.explanation: Drought is a natural cause of land degradation. Overgrazing, unsustainable farming and mining are human causes.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which type of erosion involves the development of deep channels that cannot normally be removed by ordinary tillage?

options.A: Sheet erosion
options.B: Rill erosion

questions.explanation: Gully erosion involves the development of deep channels by concentrated runoff that cannot normally be removed by ordinary tillage.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a method to reduce soil erosion on sloping land?

options.A: Overgrazing
options.B: Deforestation

questions.explanation: Terracing involves creating level or nearly level steps on sloping land to reduce runoff velocity and erosion.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is biodegradable waste?

options.A: Plastic
options.B: Glass

questions.explanation: Food scraps are biodegradable waste. Plastic, glass and metal are generally non-biodegradable.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is non-biodegradable waste?

options.A: Vegetable peels
options.B: Garden waste

questions.explanation: Plastic is generally non-biodegradable. Vegetable peels, garden waste and food scraps are biodegradable.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a sanitary waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Paper

questions.explanation: Sanitary napkins are sanitary waste under the 2026 Rules. Food waste is wet waste, and paper and glass are dry waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a special-care waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Garden waste

questions.explanation: Expired medicines are special-care waste under the 2026 Rules. Food and garden waste are wet waste, and paper is dry waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a dry waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Vegetable peels

questions.explanation: Plastic is dry waste under the 2026 Rules. Food waste, vegetable peels and garden waste are wet waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a wet waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Paper
options.B: Glass

questions.explanation: Food waste is wet waste under the 2026 Rules. Paper, glass and metal are dry waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of CPCB?

options.A: Local collection and transport of waste
options.B: State-level enforcement through authorisations
options.D: National pollution-control coordination and technical guidance

questions.explanation: The CPCB is responsible for national pollution-control coordination and technical guidance. Local collection is the role of urban local bodies, state-level enforcement is the role of State Pollution Control Boards, and mineral conservation is the role of the Indian Bureau of Mines.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of State Pollution Control Boards?

options.A: National pollution-control coordination
options.B: Local collection and transport of waste
options.D: State-level implementation and enforcement through authorisations, consents, inspections and monitoring

questions.explanation: State Pollution Control Boards are responsible for state-level implementation and enforcement through authorisations, consents, inspections and monitoring.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of urban local bodies in waste management?

options.A: National pollution-control coordination
options.B: State-level enforcement through authorisations
options.D: Local collection, segregation, transport, processing and disposal systems

questions.explanation: Urban local bodies are responsible for local collection, segregation, transport, processing and disposal systems, and enforcement of applicable municipal rules.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of sustainable development?

options.A: Economic development
options.B: Social inclusion

questions.explanation: The three pillars of sustainable development are economic development, social inclusion and environmental protection. Industrial expansion is not one of the pillars.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes intergenerational equity?

options.A: Fair distribution of resources among people of the same generation
options.B: Fairness between developed and developing countries
options.C: Equal distribution of income within a generation
options.D: Fairness between present and future generations in the use of resources and protection of the environment

questions.explanation: Intergenerational equity is fairness between present and future generations in the use of resources and protection of the environment.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes intragenerational equity?

options.A: Fairness between present and future generations
options.B: Fairness between developed and developing nations
options.C: Equal distribution of income between countries
options.D: Fair distribution of resources, opportunities, costs and benefits among people of the same generation

questions.explanation: Intragenerational equity is the fair distribution of resources, opportunities, costs and benefits among people of the same generation.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a renewable energy source?

options.A: Coal
options.B: Petroleum

questions.explanation: Solar energy is a renewable energy source. Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?

options.A: Solar
options.B: Wind

questions.explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel. Solar, wind and hydropower are renewable energy sources.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary energy source?

options.A: Coal
options.B: Crude oil

questions.explanation: Electricity is a secondary energy source produced by converting primary energy. Coal, crude oil and natural gas are primary energy sources.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary energy source?

options.A: Electricity
options.B: Petrol

questions.explanation: Coal is a primary energy source available in natural resources before conversion. Electricity, petrol and diesel are secondary energy carriers.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-commercial energy source?

options.A: Coal
options.B: Petroleum products

questions.explanation: Fuelwood is a non-commercial energy source often collected or used outside formal commercial markets. Coal, petroleum products and natural gas are commercial energy sources.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a commercial energy source?

options.A: Fuelwood
options.B: Crop residues

questions.explanation: Coal is a commercial energy source supplied through commercial markets. Fuelwood, crop residues and animal dung are non-commercial energy sources.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between energy efficiency and energy conservation?

options.A: Energy efficiency is reducing unnecessary use; energy conservation is providing the same service with less input
options.B: Both mean the same thing
options.C: Energy efficiency is capturing energy for later use; energy conservation is reducing unnecessary use
options.D: Energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input; energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures

questions.explanation: Energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input, while energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between installed capacity and electricity generation?

options.A: Installed capacity is actual energy produced; generation is rated power
options.B: Both are measured in MWh
options.D: Installed capacity is rated power; generation is actual energy produced over time

questions.explanation: Installed capacity is the rated maximum output of generating equipment, while electricity generation is the actual electrical energy produced over a period.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between primary and secondary energy?

options.A: Primary energy is produced by converting secondary energy
options.B: Secondary energy is available in natural resources before conversion
options.D: Primary energy is available in natural resources before conversion; secondary energy is produced by converting primary energy

questions.explanation: Primary energy is available in natural resources before conversion, while secondary energy is produced by converting primary energy.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between commercial and non-commercial energy?

options.A: Commercial energy is used outside formal markets; non-commercial energy is supplied through markets
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Commercial energy is traditional; non-commercial energy is modern
options.D: Commercial energy is supplied through commercial markets; non-commercial energy is often collected or used outside formal commercial markets

questions.explanation: Commercial energy is supplied through commercial markets, while non-commercial energy is traditional energy often collected or used outside formal commercial markets.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between renewable and non-fossil energy?

options.A: Renewable energy includes nuclear; non-fossil energy excludes nuclear
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Non-fossil energy is a subset of renewable energy
options.D: Renewable energy is a subset of non-fossil energy; non-fossil energy also includes nuclear

questions.explanation: Renewable energy is a subset of non-fossil energy; non-fossil energy also includes nuclear energy, which is generally not renewable.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between peak demand and capacity factor?

options.A: Peak demand is actual energy generated; capacity factor is the highest demand recorded
options.B: Both are measured in kWh
options.D: Peak demand is the highest level of electricity demand recorded; capacity factor is actual energy generated divided by the energy that could have been generated at continuous full rated capacity

questions.explanation: Peak demand is the highest level of electricity demand recorded during a specified period, while capacity factor is actual energy generated divided by the energy that could have been generated at continuous full rated capacity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between energy security and energy efficiency?

options.A: Energy security is providing the same service with less input; energy efficiency is uninterrupted availability of energy
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Energy security is reducing unnecessary use; energy efficiency is uninterrupted availability
options.D: Energy security is uninterrupted availability of energy at affordable prices; energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input

questions.explanation: Energy security is the uninterrupted availability of energy at affordable prices, with reliability, resilience and diversification. Energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between energy conservation and energy storage?

options.A: Energy conservation is capturing energy for later use; energy storage is reducing unnecessary use
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Energy conservation is providing the same service with less input; energy storage is reducing unnecessary use
options.D: Energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures; energy storage is capturing energy for later use through technologies such as pumped hydro, batteries and thermal storage

questions.explanation: Energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures, while energy storage is capturing energy for later use through technologies such as pumped hydro, batteries and thermal storage.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between grid stability and energy security?

options.A: Grid stability is uninterrupted availability of energy; energy security is maintaining frequency and voltage
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Grid stability is reducing unnecessary use; energy security is maintaining frequency
options.D: Grid stability is the ability of an electricity system to maintain frequency, voltage and reliable balance between generation and demand; energy security is uninterrupted availability of energy at affordable prices with reliability, resilience and diversification

questions.explanation: Grid stability is the ability of an electricity system to maintain frequency, voltage and reliable balance between generation and demand. Energy security is the uninterrupted availability of energy at affordable prices, with reliability, resilience and diversification.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a law with its subject?

options.A: MMDR Act, 1957 — electricity; Electricity Act, 2003 — mines
options.B: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — SEZs; SEZ Act, 2005 — environment
options.C: NGT Act, 2010 — electricity; Electricity Act, 2003 — NGT
options.D: MMDR Act, 1957 — mines and mineral development; Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — umbrella environmental framework; Electricity Act, 2003 — electricity; NGT Act, 2010 — National Green Tribunal; SEZ Act, 2005 — Special Economic Zones

questions.explanation: The MMDR Act, 1957 governs mines and mineral development; the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 provides the umbrella environmental framework; the Electricity Act, 2003 governs electricity; the NGT Act, 2010 established the National Green Tribunal; and the SEZ Act, 2005 governs Special Economic Zones.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a constitutional amendment with its subject?

options.A: 73rd Amendment — municipalities; 74th Amendment — Panchayats
options.B: 73rd Amendment — fundamental rights; 74th Amendment — directive principles

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 deals with Panchayats, and the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 deals with municipalities.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a Schedule with its subject?

options.A: Eleventh Schedule — municipal functions; Twelfth Schedule — Panchayat functions
options.B: Eleventh Schedule — fundamental duties; Twelfth Schedule — fundamental rights
options.C: Eleventh Schedule — Union List; Twelfth Schedule — State List
options.D: Eleventh Schedule — Panchayat functions; Twelfth Schedule — municipal functions

questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule lists Panchayat functions, and the Twelfth Schedule lists municipal functions.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs an institution with its function?

options.A: NITI Aayog — pollution control; CPCB — SDG India Index
options.B: Indian Bureau of Mines — geological mapping; Geological Survey of India — mineral regulation
options.C: CPCB — mineral regulation; Indian Bureau of Mines — pollution control
options.D: NITI Aayog — SDG India Index; CPCB — national pollution-control coordination; Indian Bureau of Mines — mineral regulation and conservation; Geological Survey of India — geological mapping and mineral assessment

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index; CPCB coordinates national pollution-control activities; the Indian Bureau of Mines supports mineral regulation and conservation; and the Geological Survey of India conducts geological mapping and mineral assessment.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which constitutional amendment deals with municipalities?

options.A: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
options.B: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

questions.explanation: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 deals with municipalities.

questions.question: Which type of municipality is constituted for a transitional area?

options.A: Municipal Corporation
options.B: Nagar Panchayat

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which type of municipality is constituted for a smaller urban area?

options.B: Municipal Corporation

questions.question: Which type of municipality is constituted for a larger urban area?

options.B: Municipal Council

questions.explanation: A Municipal Corporation is constituted for a larger urban area.

options.D: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea

questions.question: What is the importance of the Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway?

questions.question: What is infrastructure deficit?

questions.question: What is mining?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is a mineral?

options.A: Any material extracted from the earth
options.B: A naturally occurring inorganic substance with characteristic chemical composition and ordered internal structure, subject to legal definitions
options.D: An organic substance found in rocks

questions.explanation: A mineral is a naturally occurring inorganic substance with characteristic chemical composition and ordered internal structure, subject to legal definitions.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is an ore?

options.A: Any rock found underground
options.B: A naturally occurring material from which a mineral or metal can be extracted economically under prevailing conditions

questions.explanation: An ore is a naturally occurring material from which a mineral or metal can be extracted economically under prevailing conditions.

questions.question: What are metallic minerals?

options.A: Minerals not primarily sources of metals

questions.explanation: Metallic minerals are minerals from which metals can be extracted, such as iron ore, bauxite, manganese, copper, gold and chromite.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are non-metallic minerals?

options.A: Minerals from which metals can be extracted
options.B: Minerals not primarily sources of metals, such as limestone, mica, gypsum and dolomite

questions.explanation: Non-metallic minerals are minerals not primarily sources of metals, such as limestone, mica, gypsum and dolomite.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is open-cast mining?

options.A: Extraction through shafts and tunnels
options.B: Extraction from an open pit or surface excavation

questions.explanation: Open-cast mining is extraction from an open pit or surface excavation.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is underground mining?

options.A: Extraction from an open pit
options.B: Extraction through shafts, tunnels and underground workings

questions.explanation: Underground mining is extraction through shafts, tunnels and underground workings.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is beneficiation?

options.A: Extraction of ore from the earth
options.B: Processing ore to improve the concentration or quality of the valuable mineral

questions.explanation: Beneficiation is processing ore to improve the concentration or quality of the valuable mineral.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is overburden?

options.A: The mineral deposit itself
options.B: Soil, rock and other material lying above a mineral deposit that must be removed to access it

questions.explanation: Overburden is soil, rock and other material lying above a mineral deposit that must be removed to access it.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is mine reclamation?

options.A: Extraction of minerals from a mine
options.B: Restoration of mined land to a safe, stable condition and, where feasible, productive post-mining use
options.D: Transportation of minerals from a mine

questions.explanation: Mine reclamation is the restoration of mined land to a safe, stable condition and, where feasible, productive post-mining use.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which minerals are important in Karnataka?

options.A: Only iron ore and gold
options.B: Iron ore, gold, manganese, limestone, granite, building stone, bauxite, chromite and other industrial minerals

questions.explanation: Important minerals in Karnataka include iron ore, gold, manganese, limestone, granite, building stone, bauxite, chromite and other industrial minerals.

questions.question: What are the economic benefits of mining?

options.B: Mineral supply, employment, royalties, taxes, exports, industrial raw materials and regional economic activity

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are the environmental impacts of mining?

options.A: Mineral supply and employment
options.B: Deforestation, habitat fragmentation, dust, water contamination, groundwater changes, erosion, waste dumps, noise and landscape alteration

questions.explanation: The environmental impacts of mining include deforestation, habitat fragmentation, dust, water contamination, groundwater changes, erosion, waste dumps, noise and landscape alteration.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is illegal mining?

options.A: Mining without a licence only
options.B: Extraction or transportation violating applicable licences, leases, environmental clearances, safety rules or other legal requirements

questions.explanation: Illegal mining is extraction or transportation violating applicable licences, leases, environmental clearances, safety rules or other legal requirements.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is the District Mineral Foundation (DMF)?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is PMKKKY?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is the role of the Indian Bureau of Mines?

options.A: Geological mapping and mineral-resource assessment
options.B: Mineral conservation, mine regulation and inspection, technical studies and mineral statistics

questions.explanation: The Indian Bureau of Mines is responsible for mineral conservation, mine regulation and inspection, technical studies and mineral statistics.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is the role of the Geological Survey of India?

options.A: Mine regulation and inspection
options.B: Geological mapping, mineral-resource assessment and geoscientific investigations

questions.explanation: The Geological Survey of India is responsible for geological mapping, mineral-resource assessment and geoscientific investigations.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is land degradation?

options.A: Increase in land productivity
options.B: Decline in the biological, economic or productive capacity of land caused by natural processes or human activities
options.C: Conversion of land to urban use

questions.explanation: Land degradation is the decline in the biological, economic or productive capacity of land caused by natural processes or human activities.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is soil degradation?

options.A: Formation of new soil
options.B: Deterioration in soil quality and function, including loss of fertility, structure, organic matter or biological activity

questions.explanation: Soil degradation is the deterioration in soil quality and function, including loss of fertility, structure, organic matter or biological activity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is desertification?

options.A: The physical expansion of existing deserts
options.B: Land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas resulting from climatic variations and human activities

questions.explanation: Desertification is land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas resulting from climatic variations and human activities.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Is desertification simply the spread of deserts?

options.A: Yes. It is the physical expansion of deserts
options.B: No. It is land degradation in drylands and does not simply mean physical expansion of existing deserts
options.C: Yes. It is the formation of new deserts
options.D: No. It is the conversion of forests to deserts

questions.explanation: Desertification is land degradation in drylands and does not simply mean physical expansion of existing deserts.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is soil erosion?

options.A: Formation of new topsoil
options.B: Detachment and removal of topsoil by water, wind, ice or human activity
options.D: Accumulation of soluble salts in soil

questions.explanation: Soil erosion is the detachment and removal of topsoil by water, wind, ice or human activity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is sheet erosion?

options.A: Removal of soil by small, shallow channels
options.B: Relatively uniform removal of a thin layer of soil by surface runoff
options.C: Development of deep channels by concentrated runoff
options.D: Detachment of soil particles by wind

questions.explanation: Sheet erosion is the relatively uniform removal of a thin layer of soil by surface runoff.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is rill erosion?

options.A: Relatively uniform removal of a thin layer of soil
options.B: Removal of soil by small, shallow channels formed by concentrated runoff
options.C: Development of deep channels by concentrated runoff
options.D: Detachment of soil particles by wind

questions.explanation: Rill erosion is the removal of soil by small, shallow channels formed by concentrated runoff.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is gully erosion?

options.A: Relatively uniform removal of a thin layer of soil
options.B: Development of deep channels by concentrated runoff that cannot normally be removed by ordinary tillage
options.C: Removal of soil by small, shallow channels
options.D: Detachment of soil particles by wind

questions.explanation: Gully erosion is the development of deep channels by concentrated runoff that cannot normally be removed by ordinary tillage.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is wind erosion?

options.A: Removal of soil by water
options.B: Detachment, transport and deposition of soil particles by wind
options.D: Accumulation of soluble salts in soil

questions.explanation: Wind erosion is the detachment, transport and deposition of soil particles by wind.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is salinisation?

options.A: Removal of soluble salts from soil
options.B: Accumulation of soluble salts in soil to levels that reduce soil productivity

questions.explanation: Salinisation is the accumulation of soluble salts in soil to levels that reduce soil productivity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is waterlogging?

options.A: Accumulation of soluble salts in soil
options.B: Prolonged soil saturation that reduces air in the root zone and damages crops

questions.explanation: Waterlogging is prolonged soil saturation that reduces air in the root zone and damages crops.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is soil compaction?

options.A: Accumulation of soluble salts in soil
options.B: Compression of soil particles that reduces pore space, infiltration and root penetration

questions.explanation: Soil compaction is the compression of soil particles that reduces pore space, infiltration and root penetration.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are human causes of land degradation?

options.A: Drought, intense rainfall and floods
options.B: Deforestation, overgrazing, unsustainable farming, excessive irrigation, mining, quarrying, urban expansion, industrial pollution and improper waste disposal
options.D: Naturally occurring salinity and fragile soil conditions

questions.explanation: Human causes of land degradation include deforestation, overgrazing, unsustainable farming, excessive irrigation, mining, quarrying, urban expansion, industrial pollution and improper waste disposal.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are natural causes of land degradation?

options.A: Deforestation and overgrazing
options.B: Drought, intense rainfall, floods, landslides, wind erosion and naturally occurring salinity or fragile soil conditions

questions.explanation: Natural causes of land degradation include drought, intense rainfall, floods, landslides, wind erosion and naturally occurring salinity or fragile soil conditions.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: How does overgrazing cause degradation?

options.A: It increases soil fertility
options.B: It removes vegetation cover, exposes soil, reduces regeneration and increases erosion and compaction

questions.explanation: Overgrazing causes degradation by removing vegetation cover, exposing soil, reducing regeneration and increasing erosion and compaction.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: How can excessive irrigation degrade land?

options.A: It increases soil fertility
options.B: Poor drainage and unsuitable irrigation can cause waterlogging and salinity

questions.explanation: Excessive irrigation can degrade land because poor drainage and unsuitable irrigation can cause waterlogging and salinity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is contour ploughing?

options.A: Ploughing across contour lines
options.B: Ploughing along contour lines to slow runoff and reduce soil erosion
options.C: Ploughing in straight lines regardless of slope

questions.explanation: Contour ploughing is ploughing along contour lines to slow runoff and reduce soil erosion.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is contour bunding?

options.A: Ploughing along contour lines
options.B: Constructing embankments along contour lines to intercept runoff and conserve soil moisture
options.C: Creating level steps on sloping land
options.D: Planting rows of trees to reduce wind speed

questions.explanation: Contour bunding is constructing embankments along contour lines to intercept runoff and conserve soil moisture.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is terracing?

options.A: Ploughing along contour lines
options.B: Creating level or nearly level steps on sloping land to reduce runoff velocity and erosion
options.D: Planting rows of trees to reduce wind speed

questions.explanation: Terracing is creating level or nearly level steps on sloping land to reduce runoff velocity and erosion.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is shelterbelt planting?

options.A: Ploughing along contour lines
options.B: Planting rows of trees or shrubs to reduce wind speed and protect soil and crops
options.C: Creating level steps on sloping land

questions.explanation: Shelterbelt planting is planting rows of trees or shrubs to reduce wind speed and protect soil and crops.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is conservation agriculture?

options.A: Farming with maximum tillage
options.B: Farming based on minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover and crop diversification

questions.explanation: Conservation agriculture is farming based on minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover and crop diversification.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is land degradation neutrality?

options.A: Complete elimination of land degradation
options.B: A condition in which the amount and quality of land resources needed for ecosystem functions and services remain stable or increase over time and space
options.C: Conversion of all degraded land to forests
options.D: A condition where land degradation is allowed to continue

questions.explanation: Land degradation neutrality is a condition in which the amount and quality of land resources needed for ecosystem functions and services remain stable or increase over time and space.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is waste management?

options.A: Only collection and disposal of waste
options.B: Collection, segregation, storage, transport, processing, recovery and safe disposal of waste to protect public health and the environment

questions.explanation: Waste management is the collection, segregation, storage, transport, processing, recovery and safe disposal of waste to protect public health and the environment.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is biodegradable waste?

options.A: Waste that does not readily decompose biologically
options.B: Waste decomposed by microorganisms under suitable conditions, such as food scraps and garden waste
options.C: Waste with characteristics that pose substantial risks to human health
options.D: Waste generated during diagnosis and treatment

questions.explanation: Biodegradable waste is waste decomposed by microorganisms under suitable conditions, such as food scraps and garden waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is non-biodegradable waste?

options.A: Waste decomposed by microorganisms
options.B: Waste that does not readily decompose biologically, such as many plastics, glass and metals
options.C: Waste with characteristics that pose substantial risks to human health
options.D: Waste generated during diagnosis and treatment

questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste is waste that does not readily decompose biologically, such as many plastics, glass and metals.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is hazardous waste?

options.A: Waste decomposed by microorganisms
options.B: Waste with characteristics that can pose substantial risks to human health or the environment and is regulated under specific rules
options.C: Waste that does not readily decompose biologically
options.D: Waste generated during diagnosis and treatment

questions.explanation: Hazardous waste is waste with characteristics that can pose substantial risks to human health or the environment and is regulated under specific rules.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is biomedical waste?

options.A: Waste decomposed by microorganisms
options.B: Waste generated during diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals and related activities, as defined by applicable rules
options.C: Waste generated during construction and demolition

questions.explanation: Biomedical waste is waste generated during diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals and related activities, as defined by applicable rules.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is e-waste?

options.A: Waste generated during diagnosis and treatment
options.B: Discarded electrical and electronic equipment, including components, consumables, parts and spares
options.C: Waste generated during construction and demolition

questions.explanation: E-waste is discarded electrical and electronic equipment, including components, consumables, parts and spares.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is construction and demolition waste?

options.A: Discarded electrical and electronic equipment
options.B: Waste generated during construction, renovation, repair and demolition of buildings and civil infrastructure
options.C: Waste generated during diagnosis and treatment

questions.explanation: Construction and demolition waste is waste generated during construction, renovation, repair and demolition of buildings and civil infrastructure.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is source segregation?

options.A: Separating waste at a landfill
options.B: Separating waste where it is generated so different waste streams can be appropriately handled
options.C: Separating waste at a recycling facility

questions.explanation: Source segregation is separating waste where it is generated so different waste streams can be appropriately handled.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is the waste hierarchy?

options.A: Dispose waste first, then recycle
options.B: Prevent and reduce waste first, then reuse, recycle and recover value, with treatment and disposal as less preferred options

questions.explanation: The waste hierarchy is: prevent and reduce waste first, then reuse, recycle and recover value, with treatment and disposal as less preferred options.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is a circular economy?

options.A: An economic model based on linear production
options.B: An economic model that minimises waste and keeps products and materials in use through durability, repair, reuse, remanufacturing and recycling
options.C: An economic model based on incineration
options.D: An economic model based on landfilling

questions.explanation: A circular economy is an economic model that minimises waste and keeps products and materials in use through durability, repair, reuse, remanufacturing and recycling.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is Extended Producer Responsibility?

options.A: A policy making consumers responsible for waste disposal
options.B: A policy approach making producers responsible for collection, recycling or environmentally sound management of specified products and waste after use
options.C: A policy making local bodies responsible for waste management
options.D: A policy making recyclers responsible for waste management

questions.explanation: Extended Producer Responsibility is a policy approach making producers responsible for collection, recycling or environmentally sound management of specified products and waste after use.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is composting?

options.A: Conversion of organic waste into compost using earthworms
options.B: Controlled biological decomposition of organic waste into a stable soil-improving product
options.C: Anaerobic breakdown of biodegradable matter to produce biogas
options.D: Recovery of energy from waste through incineration

questions.explanation: Composting is the controlled biological decomposition of organic waste into a stable soil-improving product.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is vermicomposting?

options.A: Controlled biological decomposition of organic waste
options.B: Conversion of organic waste into compost using earthworms and microorganisms

questions.explanation: Vermicomposting is the conversion of organic waste into compost using earthworms and microorganisms.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is biomethanation?

options.A: Controlled biological decomposition of organic waste
options.B: Anaerobic breakdown of biodegradable matter to produce biogas and digestate
options.C: Conversion of organic waste into compost using earthworms
options.D: Recovery of energy from waste through incineration

questions.explanation: Biomethanation is the anaerobic breakdown of biodegradable matter to produce biogas and digestate.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is a material recovery facility?

options.A: A facility where wet waste is composted
options.B: A facility where dry waste is sorted and prepared for recycling or further recovery
options.C: A facility where waste is incinerated
options.D: A facility where waste is landfilled

questions.explanation: A material recovery facility is a facility where dry waste is sorted and prepared for recycling or further recovery.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is waste-to-energy?

options.A: Conversion of waste into compost
options.B: Recovery of energy from waste through processes such as incineration, refuse-derived fuel or anaerobic digestion, subject to pollution controls

questions.explanation: Waste-to-energy is the recovery of energy from waste through processes such as incineration, refuse-derived fuel or anaerobic digestion, subject to pollution controls.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is a sanitary landfill?

options.A: An open dumping ground
options.B: An engineered waste-disposal facility with controls such as liners, leachate collection, gas management, cover and monitoring

questions.explanation: A sanitary landfill is an engineered waste-disposal facility with controls such as liners, leachate collection, gas management, cover and monitoring.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is leachate?

options.A: Gas produced from waste decomposition
options.B: Contaminated liquid formed when water passes through waste and carries pollutants

questions.explanation: Leachate is contaminated liquid formed when water passes through waste and carries pollutants.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is legacy waste?

options.A: Waste generated during construction and demolition
options.B: Old accumulated waste that has remained untreated or inadequately managed at dumpsites
options.D: Waste generated during diagnosis and treatment

questions.explanation: Legacy waste is old accumulated waste that has remained untreated or inadequately managed at dumpsites.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is biomining of legacy waste?

options.A: Conversion of organic waste into compost using earthworms
options.B: Excavation, screening and processing of old dumpsite waste to recover useful fractions and reduce the volume requiring final disposal
options.D: Recovery of energy from waste through incineration

questions.explanation: Biomining of legacy waste is the excavation, screening and processing of old dumpsite waste to recover useful fractions and reduce the volume requiring final disposal.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is the umbrella framework for environmental protection and waste-management rules?

questions.explanation: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella framework for environmental protection and waste-management rules.

questions.question: What is the latest Solid Waste Management Rules framework as of November 2026?

questions.question: What is wet waste?

options.D: Specified household waste requiring careful handling

questions.question: What is dry waste?

options.C: Discarded sanitary products such as diapers and sanitary napkins
options.D: Specified household waste requiring careful handling

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is sanitary waste?

options.A: Biodegradable organic waste such as food and garden waste
options.B: Discarded sanitary products such as diapers and sanitary napkins, requiring separate safe handling
options.C: Material such as paper, plastic, glass and metal
options.D: Specified household waste requiring careful handling

questions.explanation: Sanitary waste is discarded sanitary products such as diapers and sanitary napkins, requiring separate safe handling.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What is special-care waste?

options.A: Biodegradable organic waste such as food and garden waste
options.B: Specified household waste requiring careful handling, such as certain batteries, bulbs, expired medicines, paint or pesticide containers, needles and contaminated items
options.C: Material such as paper, plastic, glass and metal
options.D: Discarded sanitary products such as diapers and sanitary napkins

questions.question: What do the 2026 Rules emphasise?

questions.question: What are the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022?

options.D: Rules prescribing segregation of biomedical waste

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022?

options.A: Rules establishing EPR for e-waste
options.B: Rules establishing EPR and environmentally sound management requirements for waste batteries
options.D: Rules prescribing segregation of biomedical waste

questions.explanation: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 establish EPR and environmentally sound management requirements for waste batteries.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are the Plastic Waste Management Rules?

options.A: Rules establishing EPR for e-waste
options.B: Rules regulating plastic-waste management and responsibilities of producers, importers, brand owners and local bodies
options.C: Rules establishing EPR for waste batteries
options.D: Rules prescribing segregation of biomedical waste

questions.explanation: The Plastic Waste Management Rules regulate plastic-waste management and responsibilities of producers, importers, brand owners and local bodies.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: What are the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016?

options.B: Rules prescribing segregation, collection, treatment and disposal requirements for biomedical waste

questions.question: What are the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for a census town under Census 2011?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a push factor of rural-to-urban migration?

options.A: Employment opportunities
options.B: Higher wages

questions.explanation: Rural unemployment is a push factor. Employment, higher wages and better education are pull factors.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a pull factor of urban migration?

options.A: Rural unemployment
options.B: Landlessness

questions.explanation: Employment opportunities are a pull factor. Rural unemployment, landlessness and drought are push factors.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive effect of urbanisation?

options.A: Housing shortages
options.B: Slums

questions.explanation: Larger markets and economic diversification are positive effects of urbanisation. Housing shortages, slums and congestion are problems of unplanned urbanisation.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a problem of unplanned urbanisation?

options.A: Productivity gains
options.B: Innovation

questions.explanation: Housing shortages and slums are problems of unplanned urbanisation. Productivity gains, innovation and economies of scale are positive effects.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an agro-based industry?

options.A: Iron and steel
options.B: Cement

questions.explanation: Sugar is an agro-based industry. Iron and steel, cement and aluminium are mineral-based industries.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a mineral-based industry?

options.A: Cotton textiles
options.B: Food processing

questions.explanation: Cement is a mineral-based industry. Cotton textiles, food processing and sugar are agro-based industries.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an adverse effect of poorly regulated industrialisation?

options.A: Employment generation
options.B: Technology transfer

questions.explanation: Air and water pollution is an adverse effect of poorly regulated industrialisation. Employment generation, technology transfer and export growth are benefits.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social infrastructure?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of economic infrastructure?

options.A: Education
options.B: Healthcare

questions.explanation: Transport is an example of economic infrastructure. Education, healthcare and housing are social infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of hard infrastructure?

options.A: Education
options.B: Healthcare

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of soft infrastructure?

options.A: Railways
options.B: Ports

questions.explanation: Education is an example of soft infrastructure. Railways, ports and power plants are hard infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-metallic mineral?

options.A: Bauxite
options.B: Manganese

questions.explanation: Limestone is a non-metallic mineral. Bauxite, manganese and copper are metallic minerals.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental impact of mining?

options.B: Royalty revenue

questions.question: Which of the following is a human cause of land degradation?

options.B: Intense rainfall

questions.question: Which of the following is a natural cause of land degradation?

options.A: Overgrazing
options.B: Unsustainable farming

questions.explanation: Drought is a natural cause of land degradation. Overgrazing, unsustainable farming and mining are human causes.

questions.question: Which type of erosion involves the development of deep channels that cannot normally be removed by ordinary tillage?

options.A: Sheet erosion

options.A: Overgrazing
options.B: Deforestation

questions.question: Which of the following is biodegradable waste?

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is non-biodegradable waste?

options.A: Vegetable peels
options.B: Garden waste

questions.explanation: Plastic is generally non-biodegradable. Vegetable peels, garden waste and food scraps are biodegradable.

options.A: Food waste

questions.question: Which of the following is a special-care waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Garden waste

questions.explanation: Expired medicines are special-care waste under the 2026 Rules. Food and garden waste are wet waste, and paper is dry waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a dry waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Vegetable peels

questions.explanation: Plastic is dry waste under the 2026 Rules. Food waste, vegetable peels and garden waste are wet waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is a wet waste stream under the 2026 Rules?

options.A: Paper
options.B: Glass

questions.explanation: Food waste is wet waste under the 2026 Rules. Paper, glass and metal are dry waste.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of CPCB?

options.D: National pollution-control coordination and technical guidance

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of State Pollution Control Boards?

options.A: National pollution-control coordination
options.B: Local collection and transport of waste

questions.explanation: State Pollution Control Boards are responsible for state-level implementation and enforcement through authorisations, consents, inspections and monitoring.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of urban local bodies in waste management?

options.A: National pollution-control coordination
options.B: State-level enforcement through authorisations
options.D: Local collection, segregation, transport, processing and disposal systems

questions.explanation: Urban local bodies are responsible for local collection, segregation, transport, processing and disposal systems, and enforcement of applicable municipal rules.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of sustainable development?

options.A: Economic development
options.B: Social inclusion

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes intergenerational equity?

options.A: Fair distribution of resources among people of the same generation
options.B: Fairness between developed and developing countries
options.C: Equal distribution of income within a generation
options.D: Fairness between present and future generations in the use of resources and protection of the environment

questions.explanation: Intergenerational equity is fairness between present and future generations in the use of resources and protection of the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes intragenerational equity?

options.A: Fairness between present and future generations
options.B: Fairness between developed and developing nations
options.C: Equal distribution of income between countries
options.D: Fair distribution of resources, opportunities, costs and benefits among people of the same generation

questions.explanation: Intragenerational equity is the fair distribution of resources, opportunities, costs and benefits among people of the same generation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?

options.B: Wind

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary energy source?

options.B: Petrol

questions.explanation: Coal is a primary energy source available in natural resources before conversion. Electricity, petrol and diesel are secondary energy carriers.

options.B: Petroleum products

questions.question: Which of the following is a commercial energy source?

options.A: Fuelwood
options.B: Crop residues

questions.explanation: Coal is a commercial energy source supplied through commercial markets. Fuelwood, crop residues and animal dung are non-commercial energy sources.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between energy efficiency and energy conservation?

options.A: Energy efficiency is reducing unnecessary use; energy conservation is providing the same service with less input
options.B: Both mean the same thing
options.C: Energy efficiency is capturing energy for later use; energy conservation is reducing unnecessary use
options.D: Energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input; energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures

questions.explanation: Energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input, while energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between installed capacity and electricity generation?

options.A: Installed capacity is actual energy produced; generation is rated power
options.B: Both are measured in MWh
options.D: Installed capacity is rated power; generation is actual energy produced over time

questions.explanation: Installed capacity is the rated maximum output of generating equipment, while electricity generation is the actual electrical energy produced over a period.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between primary and secondary energy?

options.A: Primary energy is produced by converting secondary energy
options.B: Secondary energy is available in natural resources before conversion
options.D: Primary energy is available in natural resources before conversion; secondary energy is produced by converting primary energy

questions.explanation: Primary energy is available in natural resources before conversion, while secondary energy is produced by converting primary energy.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between commercial and non-commercial energy?

options.A: Commercial energy is used outside formal markets; non-commercial energy is supplied through markets
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Commercial energy is traditional; non-commercial energy is modern
options.D: Commercial energy is supplied through commercial markets; non-commercial energy is often collected or used outside formal commercial markets

questions.explanation: Commercial energy is supplied through commercial markets, while non-commercial energy is traditional energy often collected or used outside formal commercial markets.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between renewable and non-fossil energy?

options.A: Renewable energy includes nuclear; non-fossil energy excludes nuclear
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Non-fossil energy is a subset of renewable energy
options.D: Renewable energy is a subset of non-fossil energy; non-fossil energy also includes nuclear

questions.explanation: Renewable energy is a subset of non-fossil energy; non-fossil energy also includes nuclear energy, which is generally not renewable.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between peak demand and capacity factor?

options.A: Peak demand is actual energy generated; capacity factor is the highest demand recorded
options.B: Both are measured in kWh
options.D: Peak demand is the highest level of electricity demand recorded; capacity factor is actual energy generated divided by the energy that could have been generated at continuous full rated capacity

questions.explanation: Peak demand is the highest level of electricity demand recorded during a specified period, while capacity factor is actual energy generated divided by the energy that could have been generated at continuous full rated capacity.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between energy security and energy efficiency?

options.A: Energy security is providing the same service with less input; energy efficiency is uninterrupted availability of energy
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Energy security is reducing unnecessary use; energy efficiency is uninterrupted availability
options.D: Energy security is uninterrupted availability of energy at affordable prices; energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input

questions.explanation: Energy security is the uninterrupted availability of energy at affordable prices, with reliability, resilience and diversification. Energy efficiency is providing the same energy service with less energy input.

questions.subject: Development Issues
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between energy conservation and energy storage?

options.A: Energy conservation is capturing energy for later use; energy storage is reducing unnecessary use
options.B: Both are the same
options.C: Energy conservation is providing the same service with less input; energy storage is reducing unnecessary use
options.D: Energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures; energy storage is capturing energy for later use through technologies such as pumped hydro, batteries and thermal storage

questions.explanation: Energy conservation is reducing unnecessary energy use through behavioural, technical and organisational measures, while energy storage is capturing energy for later use through technologies such as pumped hydro, batteries and thermal storage.
